newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil awards NorFra gasline contracts.
newsitem.headline: Statoil awards NorFra gasline contracts.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it had awarded contracts worth more than one billion crowns for the NorFra gas trunkline, running from the Norwegian North Sea to Dunkerque in France.
Placed on behalf of the 11-strong NorFra consortium, the agreements include a 570 million crown contract to Belgium's Jan de Nul for dredging and back-filling in the French landfall area.
A joint venture between Britain's European Marine Contractors (EMC) and Dutch HAM Contractors were awarded a deal worth 280 million crowns to trench the pipeline after laying.
EMC will be responsible for pipelaying in the landfall zone under a deal valued at 100 million crowns.
France's Spie Capag has been commissioned to lay a line from the landfall to the receiving station. Costing 80 million crowns, the section is about four km long and includes two tunnels.
NorFra will start at the Draupner E riser platform and run for 840 km at a total cost of about 10 billion crowns.
All pipelaying will be done next year with the line due to begin contractual deliveries on October 1, 1998.
Partners in the NorFra consortium are Statoil, Norsk Hydro, Saga Petroleum, Esso Norge, Mobil, Total, Elf Petroleum, Norsk Agip, Norske Shell, Neste Petroleum and Norske Conoco.
